To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Yukawa-unified supersymmetric models are consistent with the observed dark matter relic density if dark matter is a mixture of axion and axino, (2) this scenario predicts a large value for the axion mass (fa ~ 1012GeV), (3) this scenario is consistent with non-thermal leptogenisis, (4) the axion and axinos in these models can be tested at axion search and WIMP direct and indirect detection experiments, respectively.

Yukawa-unified supersymmetric models can be consistent with all cosmological, particle physics, and astrophysics data if the axion is the cold dark matter component and the axino is the warm dark matter component.

Yukawa-unified supersymmetric models with a mixed axion/ axino dark matter composition provide a viable solution to the gravitin/BBN problem while also allowing baryogenesis via leptogenesis, and are testable at current and future axion search experiments.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cosmological consequences of Yukaw-unified SUSY are rather benign and the model is consistent with all data.
Yukawa-unified supersymmetry models with axion/axion-like particles as cold and/or warm dark matter are viable models for the early and late universe.
Yukawa-unified supersymmetric models with mixed axion and axino dark matter provide a very attractive framework for cosmology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the axion/axinos can provide the dark matter of the universe in a natural way in supersymmetric models with Yukawa unification.
the axion and axino dark matter scenario in Yukawa-united SUSY models can be made consistent with cosmological and collider constraints.
